links.outcome: Model accuracy when text prompts conflict with the visual cue, and effect of Chain-of-Thought
links.effect: Overall accuracy dropped from 75% to 46% versus the visual-only condition when an inconsistent textual claim was paired with the lesion contour. CoT was associated with further degradation.
links.quote: (iii) When an overlaid lesion contour is paired with an inconsistent textual claim, the textual prompt overrides the correct visual cue: overall accuracy drops from 75% to 46% relative to the visual-only condition, and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning is associated with further degradation rather than self-correction.

unlisted_practices: Testing prompt-based strategies (one-shot text, CoT) for multimodal models for susceptibility to textual dominance over visual evidence

screen.practice: prompting strategies (one-shot text, CoT, contour overlay) as safeguards
screen.reason: Empirically tests how prompting strategies (such as one-shot and Chain-of-Thought prompting) affect diagnostic bias and safety in a medical multimodal LLM.
